title: Failure budgets and service objectives
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of failure budgets and service objectives
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: A declared measured target over a specified scope
The failures allowed under that target
A request included under the declared denominator rule

blocks.text: In the interval 200 requests are eligible and 5 fail.
195/200=97.5%, below 98%; failures exceed budget 4 by one. This is the measured interval only.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Objective 95% over 80 eligible requests. Five fail. Compute allowed failures and observed success.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Allowed four; 75/80=93.75%, so objective fails. Unknown eligibility cannot be silently excluded.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Meeting one interval objective does not establish every future interval or zero critical failures.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: For a fictional objective at least 98% of 200 eligible requests must pass all contract checks. Allowed failures are 2%*200=4. Count every eligible failure once; report excluded requests separately.
